page: Microsoft Azure FX16-4mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by an L3 cache of 260 MB. A key characteristic of this server is its massive memory capacity of 336.0 GB, translating to an exceptionally high resource density of 84.0 GB of RAM per core. It also includes 945 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong single-core profile alongside moderate multi-core capabilities. The server achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2357.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (34.85 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.39 GB/sec). However, due to the low core count, multi-core benchmarks are relatively limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression both landing in the weak tier. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only speed of 345.84 GB/sec for small cached blocks, but uncached large-block read and write speeds are weaker, measuring 36.33 GB/sec and 25.55 GB/sec respectively.

The primary tradeoff of the FX16-4mds_v2 is its extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio, which provides massive RAM capacity but limits parallel processing power due to having only 4 vCPUs. This makes it highly cost-efficient for workloads that require large memory footprints but do not scale heavily with core counts. It is well-suited for memory-intensive database operations, caching layers like Redis (achieving 6.34 million SET operations per second in benchmarks), and single-threaded data processing tasks. It is less suitable for highly parallelized multi-threaded compute tasks, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference.
